## Default-flag flip exposes latent opt-in-branch defect (P1, Python)

Pattern: a change flips a module-level default (e.g. `DETAILED_REPORT = False -> True`) so a branch that was previously opt-in now runs on the default call path. Any latent boundary bug in that branch (here: `sum(values) / len(values)` with no empty-list guard -> ZeroDivisionError) becomes a regression for every default caller, even though the diff touches only a constant and a test expectation.

Review heuristic: when a diff flips a default flag, enumerate the boundary inputs the contract promises for BOTH modes (empty collections, zero counts, None) and run the newly-default branch on them. Tests that only update the populated-input expectation do not cover this. Fix belongs in the branch (guard the boundary), plus a default-mode boundary test.
